closed_children.title: UI skeleton: lernie-ui-egui binary + Cargo wiring

description:
Milestone per ARCHITECTURE.md §12 v0.5.

Success criterion (quoted): Git tree view, live streaming, pulsing tool indicators, branch-state indicators. Tailing the event log is the only read mechanism. [The 'tailing' phrasing is being retired by bl-bcd9 — the real mechanism is filesystem watching. Success criterion is restated below against the revised arch.]

=== Restated success criterion (post bl-bcd9) ===

A Dioxus-based frontend that, against a live conversation repo:
- Renders a git tree view of exchanges, invocations, and merges.
- Shows live streaming text for in-flight model calls.
- Shows pulsing indicators for in-flight tool calls.
- Shows branch-state indicators (in-flight, merged, stopped, conflicted).
- Issues user actions (new prompt, stop, resume) exclusively via 'lernie <subcommand>' invocations.
- Holds no persistent state: every render is a pure function of filesystem state at the current git ref.

=== Stack ===

Dioxus (pure Rust programming model; webview runtime via Tao/Wry, same as Tauri). Chosen over egui because Dioxus decouples component state from pixel layout cleanly, which matches the strict-statelessness requirement.

=== Contract (pinned by bl-bcd9) ===

Frontend reads and watches paths under the conversation repo. Frontend writes nothing to the repo. Frontend→harness commands go exclusively through 'lernie <subcommand>' invocations. Multiple frontends may run concurrently against one repo. See §3 / §7 of ARCHITECTURE.md for the enumerated surface once bl-bcd9 lands.

=== Hard dependencies (do these first) ===

- bl-bcd9 — ARCH doc revision. Blocks anything that depends on the frontend/backend contract being pinned down.
- bl-4772 (v0.2 git tree) — needed for anything involving exchange branches, branch-state indicators, no-ff merge topology rendering. Without v0.2, there are no branches to render; only v0.1's flat 'commit on main' shape exists.
- v0.3 epic (tools, not yet filed) — needed for pulsing tool-call indicators and tool output rendering.
- v0.4 epic (invocations, not yet filed) — needed for sub-branch arrows to live invocations and the nested-tree view.

User's standing direction: if this epic has dependencies, note them, and the earlier epics get done first. So this epic is filed as a roadmap anchor; actual claim happens once bl-bcd9 + bl-4772 are merged.

=== Parallel-ok work that could start before deps ship ===

If we want to move sooner, the following subtasks do NOT depend on v0.2+ and could be claimed once bl-bcd9 merges:
- Dioxus skeleton: Cargo wiring, basic window, no-op render.
- Filesystem watcher: inotify + polling fallback (ARCH §3.1), isolated module with its own tests.
- CLI outbound wrapper: thin Rust abstraction that exec's 'lernie <subcommand>' and streams stdout/stderr back; reusable by any future frontend.
- Git tree renderer against v0.1-shape repos: renders the flat 'one commit per exchange on main' shape that v0.1 already produces. Extends naturally when v0.2 adds branches.

These can be filed as subtasks under this epic once bl-bcd9 is merged; leaving them latent until then.

=== Out of scope ===

- History-view forking from old commits (v1, not v0.5 — flagged in ARCH §7.2).
- Workflow-config UI (v0.6).
- Task-suite UI (v0.7).
- Replay/tarball UI (v0.8).
- Embedding in another tool — that's the standing 'exec lernie' pattern, no UI work required.

=== Testing strategy ===

Per AGENTS.md: 'if it can't be tested, it mustn't be built.' The stateless-frontend discipline makes most of this testable without pixels:
- Renderer functions take (filesystem snapshot) -> (view model). Unit-test against real fixtures (small, hand-constructed lernie repos on disk — not mocks).
- Filesystem watcher tested against real tmpfs events.
- CLI outbound tested against a fake 'lernie' binary on PATH (shell stub), no mocking of the Rust call site.
- Dioxus component tests for the rsx!-level logic via Dioxus's built-in testing harness. Pixel-level smoke tests gated behind a feature flag so CI can run them only in environments with a webview available.

100% coverage per repo precommit hooks.

=== Done-when ===

End-to-end demo: open a fresh conversation repo, run 'lernie prompt <repo> \"hello\"' in one terminal, and the live frontend renders the exchange branch spawning, the streaming response, the merge back to main, with branch-state indicators flipping through in-flight → merged. Kill the process mid-stream and see the stopped marker.

All subtask gates closed. cargo test + tarpaulin --fail-under 100 green on merge.
title: v0.5: UI (Dioxus frontend)
